review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of `full` and `restrictedNormDiagram_map` in RestrictedLevelCompactFunctoriality.lean. The only duplicated proof I found that I'd call well-supported is `fullNorm_map_coe` versus `normDiagram_map_coe`. Other repeated `congrArg (fun t => (t.1 : …))` extractions are short routine plumbing, so I did not report them. I could not run Lean. I believe the specialization `normDiagram_map_coe (full A)` typechecks, because `full A` has `toLevelCompactRep := A` and the projections reduce definitionally. That is untested.

findings.problem: `fullNorm_map_coe` is the statement of `normDiagram_map_coe` (lines 207-227) with `B := full A`, and its proof is the same step-for-step. Both take `ConcreteCategory.congr_hom` of `restrictedNormDiagram_map` and push it through the `.1` projection with `congrArg`. Both then run the same three-step calc through `relativeNormHom`, `relativeNormHom_apply` and `relativeNorm_coe`. Since `full A` has `toLevelCompactRep := A`, we get `(full A).rep = A.rep` definitionally. The only difference is that the full-system version is stated and proved separately, earlier in the file. A later use at line 259 passes `B.toLevelCompactRep`, which is exactly the instance `normDiagram_map_coe (full B.toLevelCompactRep)` would cover.
findings.proposed_change: Move `normDiagram_map_coe` (generic in `B : RestrictedLevelCompactRep R G`) above `fullNorm_map_coe` and delete the second 20-line proof. If the name is still wanted, replace it with a one-line specialization: `private theorem fullNorm_map_coe (A) (U V) (hVU) (y) : ... := normDiagram_map_coe (full A) U V hVU y`. Alternatively, drop it and call `normDiagram_map_coe (full A)` at lines 81, 88, 159 and 259. The statement may need a `show` or `by exact` if elaboration does not unfold `(full A).rep` automatically.
findings.benefit: One proof of the key fact that the diagram map on underlying invariants is the relative norm replaces two copies. A future change to `relativeNormHom` or `restrictedNormDiagram` needs fixing in one place, and the reader no longer has to check that two near-identical calc blocks agree.
